description: List the objects a workspace defines — companies, people, deals, and every custom object — as the options a person picks from. Each option's id is the object's api_slug, which is what attio-list_records-1, attio-create_records-1 and attio-update_records-1 take as `object`. Attio returns every object in one answer, so there is no cursor. This is the browse node behind the attio sync picker, so its output is the scope-option shape.

parent_id.description: Ignored. Objects are a flat list, so there is nothing to open.

query.description: Ignored. GET /v2/objects takes no filter; see quirks.

cursor.description: Ignored. Attio returns every object in one answer.

limit.description: Ignored. GET /v2/objects takes no page size.

next_cursor.description: Always null. Attio lists every object in one answer.

response_schema.description: Lenient ingress on GET /v2/objects, from Attio's published OpenAPI document. Attio marks api_slug, singular_noun and plural_noun nullable, so the mapping below never assumes one is there.

quirks: No code: the whole call is a declarative http mapping. GET /v2/objects takes no parameter and answers with every object, so there is nothing to build and nothing to page.

The option id is the api_slug, not the object_id, because that is what every other Attio node takes as `object` and what a crawler must be able to use straight out of sync_scope. Attio marks api_slug nullable, so the mapping falls back to the object_id, which the other nodes also accept.
The label prefers plural_noun — People, Companies — because a picker lists many of a thing. singular_noun, the slug and the id follow it, so a row always reads as something.
No sublabel: the api_slug is already the id the picker shows, and a null one would be a null where the option shape wants text.
The four value-expression operators cannot filter, so `query` is accepted and ignored. A workspace has tens of objects, not thousands, so the picker can filter what it already fetched.
